SECTION: Chapter 1: Hardware Installation (Pages 5-8)

TOPICS: hardware installation, cable connections, power setup, power modes, remote control, on-screen display navigation

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- To access connectors, remove the connector cover after disconnecting the power cord (Page 5)
- Only remove the four screws affixing the connector cover; removing others may cause electric shock (Page 5)
- The device has 15 labeled ports on its rear panel, including 24 V DC In, Dual DVI in, HDMI 1.4, DP1.2 Out, VGA In, HDMI 2.0, SDI In, SDI Out, RJ-11, Mic In, Line Out, RS-232, USB 2.0, and Power 5V Out (Page 5)
- Several video and/or data cables can be connected in many combinations, with the number and type automatically detected by the monitor (Page 6)
- The user can select the image display method from the OSD (On Screen Display) (Page 6)
- A secure connection is important for best image quality, requiring tightened thumb screws on video cables (Page 6)
- Section 1.3 describes the Ground Pin, which connects the monitor to Protective Earth and can be used for potential equalization with other equipment (Page 6)
- For potential equalization, connect the POAG pin on devices to the monitor's ground pin using an AWG18 wire (WIRE NOT PROVIDED) (Page 6)
- Section 1.4 outlines four steps for connecting power: connect the AC cord to the AC IN terminal, connect the DC OUT terminal of the AC adaptor to the DC IN terminal on the monitor, align the notch on the cord connector with the guiding groove, and plug the AC cord plug into the power outlet (Page 6)
- Hard power and soft power are used independently (Page 7)
- To turn on hard power, turn the POWER switch to On; the indicator glows blue (Page 7)
- To turn off hard power, turn the POWER switch to off; the indicator light turns off (Page 7)
- The soft power button enables or disables the video screen with one touch (Page 7)
- There may be a few-second delay in displaying an image after pressing the soft power button (Page 7)
- The table shows LED light combinations and their meanings for various power states (Page 7)
- All monitor controls can be accessed through the IR remote control (Page 8)
- The Soft Power key initiates the Quick Menu (Page 8)
- The Central Key contains Volume increase/decrease, down/less, up/more, and enter functions (Page 8)
- The PIP Key initiates Picture in Picture Features (Page 8)
- The Source Key initiates the next active video input (Page 8)
- The Zoom In Key initiates Zoom In (Page 8)
- The Swap Key initiates an image swap during a 2P mode (Page 8)
- The Mute Key activates or deactivates speakers (Page 8)
- The Zoom Out Key initiates Zoom out (Page 8)
- Pressing the Enter key opens the OSD menu (Page 8)
- The table shows the response after touching different OSD icons (Page 8)

SECTION: Chapter 2: Operating the Device (Pages 8-19)

TOPICS: IR remote control, On-Screen Display (OSD) menu navigation, OSD locking, Quick Key function, color schemes and profiles, display adjustments, audio settings, multi-display modes, Picture-in-Picture (PIP), monitor information, advanced settings

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- All monitor controls can be accessed through the IR remote control. (Page 8)
- The Soft Power key initiates the Quick Menu. (Page 8)
- The Central Key contains Volume increase/decrease, down/less, up/more, and enter functions. (Page 8)
- The PIP Key initiates Picture in Picture Features. (Page 8)
- The Source Key initiates the next active video input. (Page 8)
- The Zoom In Key initiates Zoom In. (Page 8)
- The Swap Key initiates an image swap during a 2P mode. (Page 8)
- The Mute Key activates or deactivates speakers. (Page 8)
- The Zoom Out Key initiates Zoom out. (Page 8)
- Pressing the Enter key opens the OSD menu. (Page 8)
- Touching both the $\odot$ and $\oplus$ buttons simultaneously turns ON or OFF the OSD lockout feature. (Page 9)
- Touching either the $\odot$ or $\oplus$ button initiates the brightness control feature. (Page 9)
- The QUICK key offers easier access to six major monitor adjustments. (Page 9)
- The SOURCE 1 sub-menu allows selection of video sources including VGA, DVI, HDMI 2.0, HDMI 1.4, DP, and SDI. (Page 9)
- The ZOOM sub-menu allows selection of which image to zoom into and includes options for ZOOM IN, ZOOM H POSITION, ZOOM V POSITION, and ZOOM SOURCE. (Page 9)
- The SCHEME sub-menu offers six (6) color schemes to choose from. (Page 10)
- Each color scheme can be adjusted individually under the OSD function DISPLAY, menu option SCHEME ADJUST. (Page 10)
- The primary colors and secondary colors are adjustable. (Page 10)
- Under Profile, the sub-menu offers six (6) different previously saved 3D LUT (Look Up Table) profiles to select from. (Page 10)
- Profile can be uploaded using the Tomlinson Color calibration software (not included). (Page 10)
- The Profile menu shows options for MEDICAL, CUSTOM 1, CUSTOM 2, CUSTOM 3, CUSTOM 4, and CUSTOM 5. (Page 10)
- The OSD offers various monitor adjustment capabilities. (Page 11)
- Under SCHEME ADJUST, HUE and Saturation of each primary and secondary color can be changed, stored under the current scheme. (Page 11)
- Changes in COLOR CONTROL do not overwrite the setting of SCHEME or PROFILE. (Page 11)
- The REGION function allows selection of "region(s)" / input(s) to adjust. (Page 11)
- An example states there are nine (9) possible region combinations for a monitor with four inputs on a quad screen, and only quadrant "1" will receive adjustment. (Page 11)
- The Brightness setting adjusts overall image and background brightness with a value range of 0-100. (Page 12)
- The Temperature setting adjusts color temperature with options including USER, 5600, 6500, 7600, and 9300 Kelvin. (Page 12)
- The Gamma setting offers Native 1.8, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4, or DICOM (Optional) values, with DICOM being calibratable via optional software. (Page 12)
- The Region setting allows selection of multi-source configurations like 1P, 1/2P, 2/2P, and combinations up to 4/4P. (Page 12)
- The ADJUST feature automatically adjusts an analog image. (Page 13)
- When an analog image is initially detected, the monitor will attempt to automatically adjust the image positioning. (Page 13)
- The automatic adjustment feature can be turned On/Off via the menu. (Page 13)
- White balance can be adjusted automatically by selecting "WHITE BALANCE" and pressing ENTER. (Page 13)
- The speaker volume for all audio inputs is controlled in the Basic OSD Menu. (Page 14)
- The AUDIO SOURCE option allows the user to select which input to use. (Page 14)
- There are 3 regions within the Quad display with audio. (Page 14)
- The AUTO Adjust function automatically adjusts screen size, H position, V position, Clock, and Clock Phase when the video source changes. (Page 14)
- All adjustment values (H Position, V Position, Clock, Phase) have a range of 0-100. (Page 14)
- Section 2.9 is titled "Basic OSD Menu Options: Multi-Display". (Page 15)
- Display mode offers up to five different layouts to view input images. (Page 15)
- Volume adjusts level from 0-100 with decrease/increase controls. (Page 15)
- Mute has ON/OFF toggle. (Page 15)
- Audio Source can be selected from Audio IN, Fiber, 1P, 2P, 3P, 4P. (Page 15)
- Each source can be assigned an active image, but only one source can be set to auto scan. (Page 15)
- Under the PIP layout position and size of the inner image can be adjusted. (Page 16)
- Selecting MONITOR INFO displays the current state of the monitor, including PCB version, firmware version, serial number, and inputs. (Page 17)
- The OSD Turn Off setting controls the auto-close time, with a value range of 0-60 seconds. (Page 17)
- The OSD Position can be adjusted from 0-100 for horizontal and vertical placement. (Page 17)
- The OSD Transparency level is adjustable from 0-255. (Page 17)
- The OSD Rotated setting allows rotation at 0°, 90°, or 270°. (Page 17)
- In the ADVANCED menu, selecting SCALING lets the user choose the image perspective. (Page 17)
- The ability to control the monitor's functions via an infrared remote can be enabled or disabled. (Page 18)
- The "ADVANCED" menu contains options for Scaling, Flip, Overscan, RGB/YUV, RS232, Touch, Ambient Sensor, IR Sensor, DP EDID, and Factory Reset. (Page 18)
- Specific settings include scaling ratios (Full/16:10/16:9/4:3/5:4/1:1), flip modes (Rotate 0/90/180/270/LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN), overscan types (Under scan, Over Scan), and DP EDID resolutions (1080P, 4K2K 30Hz, 4K2K 60Hz). (Page 18)
- The Factory Reset option resets the OSD options back to factory settings with a Yes/No confirmation. (Page 18)
- The LCD Monitor is intended for 4K 2D color video display from endoscopic/laparoscopic systems and other compatible healthcare imaging systems. (Page 19)
- For U.S. customers, the equipment complies with FCC Rules part 15 as a Class B digital device, with two conditions: it may not cause harmful interference and must accept any interference received. (Page 19)

SECTION: Chapter 2: Operating the Device (Pages 8-19)

TOPICS: IR remote control, On-Screen Display (OSD) menu navigation, OSD locking, Quick Key function, color schemes and profiles, display adjustments, audio settings, multi-display modes, Picture-in-Picture (PIP), monitor information, advanced settings

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- All monitor controls can be accessed through the IR remote control. (Page 8)
- The Soft Power key initiates the Quick Menu. (Page 8)
- The Central Key contains Volume increase/decrease, down/less, up/more, and enter functions. (Page 8)
- The PIP Key initiates Picture in Picture Features. (Page 8)
- The Source Key initiates the next active video input. (Page 8)
- The Zoom In Key initiates Zoom In. (Page 8)
- The Swap Key initiates an image swap during a 2P mode. (Page 8)
- The Mute Key activates or deactivates speakers. (Page 8)
- The Zoom Out Key initiates Zoom out. (Page 8)
- Pressing the Enter key opens the OSD menu. (Page 8)
- Touching both the $\odot$ and $\oplus$ buttons simultaneously turns ON or OFF the OSD lockout feature. (Page 9)
- Touching either the $\odot$ or $\oplus$ button initiates the brightness control feature. (Page 9)
- The QUICK key offers easier access to six major monitor adjustments. (Page 9)
- The SOURCE 1 sub-menu allows selection of video sources including VGA, DVI, HDMI 2.0, HDMI 1.4, DP, and SDI. (Page 9)
- The ZOOM sub-menu allows selection of which image to zoom into and includes options for ZOOM IN, ZOOM H POSITION, ZOOM V POSITION, and ZOOM SOURCE. (Page 9)
- The SCHEME sub-menu offers six (6) color schemes to choose from. (Page 10)
- Each color scheme can be adjusted individually under the OSD function DISPLAY, menu option SCHEME ADJUST. (Page 10)
- The primary colors and secondary colors are adjustable. (Page 10)
- Under Profile, the sub-menu offers six (6) different previously saved 3D LUT (Look Up Table) profiles to select from. (Page 10)
- Profile can be uploaded using the Tomlinson Color calibration software (not included). (Page 10)
- The Profile menu shows options for MEDICAL, CUSTOM 1, CUSTOM 2, CUSTOM 3, CUSTOM 4, and CUSTOM 5. (Page 10)
- The OSD offers various monitor adjustment capabilities. (Page 11)
- Under SCHEME ADJUST, HUE and Saturation of each primary and secondary color can be changed, stored under the current scheme. (Page 11)
- Changes in COLOR CONTROL do not overwrite the setting of SCHEME or PROFILE. (Page 11)
- The REGION function allows selection of "region(s)" / input(s) to adjust. (Page 11)
- An example states there are nine (9) possible region combinations for a monitor with four inputs on a quad screen, and only quadrant "1" will receive adjustment. (Page 11)
- The Brightness setting adjusts overall image and background brightness with a value range of 0-100. (Page 12)
- The Temperature setting adjusts color temperature with options including USER, 5600, 6500, 7600, and 9300 Kelvin. (Page 12)
- The Gamma setting offers Native 1.8, 2.0, 2.2, 2.4, or DICOM (Optional) values, with DICOM being calibratable via optional software. (Page 12)
- The Region setting allows selection of multi-source configurations like 1P, 1/2P, 2/2P, and combinations up to 4/4P. (Page 12)
- The ADJUST feature automatically adjusts an analog image. (Page 13)
- When an analog image is initially detected, the monitor will attempt to automatically adjust the image positioning. (Page 13)
- The automatic adjustment feature can be turned On/Off via the menu. (Page 13)
- White balance can be adjusted automatically by selecting "WHITE BALANCE" and pressing ENTER. (Page 13)
- The speaker volume for all audio inputs is controlled in the Basic OSD Menu. (Page 14)
- The AUDIO SOURCE option allows the user to select which input to use. (Page 14)
- There are 3 regions within the Quad display with audio. (Page 14)
- The AUTO Adjust function automatically adjusts screen size, H position, V position, Clock, and Clock Phase when the video source changes. (Page 14)
- All adjustment values (H Position, V Position, Clock, Phase) have a range of 0-100. (Page 14)
- Section 2.9 is titled "Basic OSD Menu Options: Multi-Display". (Page 15)
- Display mode offers up to five different layouts to view input images. (Page 15)
- Volume adjusts level from 0-100 with decrease/increase controls. (Page 15)
- Mute has ON/OFF toggle. (Page 15)
- Audio Source can be selected from Audio IN, Fiber, 1P, 2P, 3P, 4P. (Page 15)
- Each source can be assigned an active image, but only one source can be set to auto scan. (Page 15)
- Under the PIP layout position and size of the inner image can be adjusted. (Page 16)
- Selecting MONITOR INFO displays the current state of the monitor, including PCB version, firmware version, serial number, and inputs. (Page 17)
- The OSD Turn Off setting controls the auto-close time, with a value range of 0-60 seconds. (Page 17)
- The OSD Position can be adjusted from 0-100 for horizontal and vertical placement. (Page 17)
- The OSD Transparency level is adjustable from 0-255. (Page 17)
- The OSD Rotated setting allows rotation at 0°, 90°, or 270°. (Page 17)
- In the ADVANCED menu, selecting SCALING lets the user choose the image perspective. (Page 17)
- The ability to control the monitor's functions via an infrared remote can be enabled or disabled. (Page 18)
- The "ADVANCED" menu contains options for Scaling, Flip, Overscan, RGB/YUV, RS232, Touch, Ambient Sensor, IR Sensor, DP EDID, and Factory Reset. (Page 18)
- Specific settings include scaling ratios (Full/16:10/16:9/4:3/5:4/1:1), flip modes (Rotate 0/90/180/270/LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN), overscan types (Under scan, Over Scan), and DP EDID resolutions (1080P, 4K2K 30Hz, 4K2K 60Hz). (Page 18)
- The Factory Reset option resets the OSD options back to factory settings with a Yes/No confirmation. (Page 18)
- The LCD Monitor is intended for 4K 2D color video display from endoscopic/laparoscopic systems and other compatible healthcare imaging systems. (Page 19)
- For U.S. customers, the equipment complies with FCC Rules part 15 as a Class B digital device, with two conditions: it may not cause harmful interference and must accept any interference received. (Page 19)
- All interface cables used to connect peripherals must be shielded to comply with FCC Rules Subpart B of part 15. (Page 19)
- The product is manufactured by Winmate Inc. and certified per Standard CAN/CSA-C22.2 No.60601-1. (Page 19)
- All equipment connected to this unit must be certified per Standard IEC60601-1, IEC60950-1, IEC60065, or other applicable IEC/ISO Standards. (Page 19)

pages.ocr_text: 2.6 Basic OSD Menu Options: Display The OSD offers a variety of monitor adjustment capabilities. Below is a description of a few common functions used. Under SCHEME ADJUST, the HUE and Saturation of each primary and secondary color can be changed. These changes are stored under the SCHEME currently activated. (Found under the Quick Menu) Under COLOR CONTROL, the RED, GREEN, and BLUE colors of the current image are changed. These adjustments DO NOT over write the setting of SCHEME or PROFILE. Region allows the user to select the "region(s)" / input(s) to adjust with a feature. Example: Monitor has four inputs signals activated on a quad screen. There are nine (9) possible region combinations that can be adjusted. In the picture below, only quadrant "1" will receive adjustment.
pages.summary:
This page (Page 10) details the basic OSD menu options for display adjustments, focusing on three main functions: Scheme Adjust, Color Control, and Region. It explains that Scheme Adjust modifies the hue and saturation of primary and secondary colors, with changes saved under the active scheme. Color Control allows independent adjustment of red, green, and blue color channels without overwriting the scheme or profile settings. The Region function enables users to select specific input regions for adjustment, illustrated by an example where a quad screen has nine possible combinations, but only quadrant "1" is being adjusted. Two figures show the corresponding OSD menus for these functions.

**Text Evidence:**
- The OSD offers various monitor adjustment capabilities.
- Under SCHEME ADJUST, HUE and Saturation of each primary and secondary color can be changed, stored under the current scheme.
- Changes in COLOR CONTROL do not overwrite the setting of SCHEME or PROFILE.
- The REGION function allows selection of "region(s)" / input(s) to adjust.
- An example states there are nine (9) possible region combinations for a monitor with four inputs on a quad screen, and only quadrant "1" will receive adjustment.

It features a screenshot of the on-screen display (OSD) menu highlighting the "ADVANCED" tab and lists various configuration options in a table format. The table includes settings for image scaling, flipping, overscan, color space (RGB/YUV), RS232 and Touch signal sources, ambient and IR sensors, DP EDID resolution and refresh rate, and a factory reset function. The primary purpose is to guide users through configuring these specific monitor functions.

TOPICS: regulatory compliance, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), safety warnings, installation precautions, power supply requirements, display technology, troubleshooting, technical specifications

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The LCD Monitor is intended for 4K 2D color video display from endoscopic/laparoscopic systems and other compatible healthcare imaging systems (Page 19)
- For U.S. customers, the equipment complies with FCC Rules part 15 as a Class B digital device, requiring shielded cables and acceptance of any interference received (Page 19)
- The product is manufactured by Winmate Inc. and certified per Standard CAN/CSA-C22.2 No.60601-1 (Page 19)
- All equipment connected to this unit must be certified per Standard IEC60601-1, IEC60950-1, IEC60065, or other applicable IEC/ISO Standards (Page 19)
- The M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX requires special precautions for EMC and must be installed per the instructions for use (Page 20)
- Portable and mobile RF communications equipment such as cellular phones can affect the M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX (Page 20)
- Using accessories and cables other than those specified may result in increased emissions or decreased immunity (Page 20)
- The device is intended for use in the electromagnetic environment specified in the table (Page 20)
- All configurations must comply with the system standard IEC60601-1-1 (Page 20)
- The M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX is intended for use in an electromagnetic environment specified below (Page 21)
- For ESD, the test level is ±6 kV contact and ±8 kV air, with compliance required at the same levels (Page 21)
- For Electrical Fast Transient/Burst, the test level is ±2 kV for power supply lines and ±1 kV for input/output lines (Page 21)
- For Surge, the test level is ±1 kV line-to-line and ±2 kV line-to-earth (Page 21)
- For Voltage Dips, Short Interruptions, and Voltage Variations, the test levels are <5% dip for 0.5 cycle, 40% dip for 5 cycles, and 70% dip for 25 cycles (Page 21)
- For Power Frequency Magnetic Field, the test level is 3 A/m (Page 21)
- The customer or user should assure the device is used in the specified environment (Page 21)
- If continued operation during power interruptions is required, it is recommended to power the device from an uninterruptible power supply or battery (Page 21)
- The M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX is intended for use in the specified electromagnetic environment (Page 22)
- Conducted RF test level is 3 Vrms from 150 kHz to 80 MHz (Page 22)
- Radiated RF test level is 3 V/m from 80 MHz to 2.5 GHz (Page 22)
- Recommended separation distance is calculated using the formula d = [3.5/v₁]√p for 80 MHz to 800 MHz and d = [7/E₁]√p for 80 MHz to 2.5 GHz (Page 22)
- NOTE 1 states that at 80 MHz and 800 MHz, the higher frequency range applies (Page 22)
- NOTE 2 explains that guidelines may not apply in all situations due to absorption and reflection (Page 22)
- The M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX is intended for use in controlled electromagnetic environments (Page 23)
- Recommended separation distances are provided to prevent electromagnetic interference (Page 23)
- For transmitters not listed, the separation distance can be estimated using the formula d = [constant] * √P (Page 23)
- NOTE 1 states that at 80 MHz and 800 MHz, the higher frequency range applies (Page 23)
- NOTE 2 states these guidelines may not apply in all situations due to absorption and reflection (Page 23)
- The apparatus must not be exposed to dripping or splashing liquids (Page 24)
- The unit must be firmly fixed to the floor or wall to prevent injuries (Page 24)
- When using the M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX adjacent to or stacked with other equipment, normal operation must be verified (Page 24)
- Disposal of the unit must comply with local laws and hospital regulations regarding environmental pollution (Page 24)
- Installation space must allow for ventilation and service, with specific clearances: 4 cm (1 5/8 inches) behind, 10 cm (4 inches) from left and right sides, 6 cm (2 3/8 inches) from the bottom, and 30 cm (11 7/8 inches) above the unit (Page 24)
- A warning on power connection requires using a proper, approved 3-core mains lead with earthing contacts that conforms to local safety regulations and proper voltage/ampere ratings (Page 24)
- For customers in U.S.A. and Canada, use a power supply cord with a HOSPITAL GRADE* plug (Page 25)
- Grounding reliability requires connection to a receptacle marked "Hospital Only" or "Hospital Grade" (Page 25)
- The unit is heavy; unpack and move with two or more people (Page 25)
- The device (M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX) is DC powered and requires an AC adapter (EM11701F) (Page 25)
- Operate the unit on 100-240V AC only (Page 25)
- Unplug the unit if not used for several days or more (Page 25)
- To disconnect the AC power cord, pull out by grasping the plug, not the cord itself (Page 25)
- Prevent internal heat build-up by allowing adequate air circulation (Page 25)
- Do not place the unit on surfaces like rugs or blankets, or near materials that block ventilation holes (Page 25)
- Do not install the unit near heat sources, direct sunlight, excessive dust, mechanical vibration, or shock (Page 25)
- Do not place the monitor near equipment generating magnetism, such as transformers or high-voltage power lines (Page 25)
- Users should check for discomfort before using the monitor in healthcare practice (Page 26)
- Electrosurgical knives can cause picture disturbance due to strong radio waves or voltages, which is not a malfunction (Page 26)
- Problems can occur during critical use, so using more than one unit or having a spare is strongly recommended (Page 26)
- The LCD panel has a functioning pixel ratio of at least 99.99% (Page 26)
- A residual image may appear if the unit is used in a cold place, but this is not a malfunction (Page 26)
- The screen and cabinet become warm during operation, which is normal (Page 26)
- Burn-in can be caused by masked/boarded images with aspect ratios other than 16:9, color bars, or continuous characters (Page 27)
- To reduce burn-in risk, turn off character displays from connected equipment (Page 27)
- The screen protect panel is made of toughened glass but may crack from strong impact or scratching (Page 27)
- Moisture condensation occurs when the unit moves from cold to warm environments; operating during condensation may damage the unit (Page 27)
- Cleaning requires disconnecting the AC power cord before starting (Page 27)
- The front protection plate withstands disinfection and is treated to reduce light reflection (Page 27)
- Use 50-70% isopropyl alcohol or 76.9-81.4% ethanol for cleaning, wiping with less than 1 N force (Page 27)
- Avoid solvents like benzene, thinners, acid, alkaline, abrasive detergents, or chemical cleaning cloths (Page 27)
- Do not use solvents such as benzene, thinner, acid, alkaline, or abrasive detergents for cleaning (Page 28)
- The device is suitable for healthcare environments due to its easy-to-clean structure and materials (Page 28)
- Normal use must exclude biological contaminated environments to prevent infection spread (Page 28)
- Returned products must be decontaminated per the latest ANSI/AAMI ST35 standard (Page 28)
- At least one adhesive yellow label and a declaration statement proving decontamination are required for returns (Page 28)
- Products without the required label or declaration can be rejected and shipped back at the Customer's expense (Page 28)
- Section 3.8 is titled "Frequency Table" (Page 29)
- The table covers signal names including 640 x 480, 480P, 800 x 600, 1024 x 768, 720P, 1280 x 1024, 1600 x 1200, 1920 x 1080, 1920 x 1200, 2560 x 1440, 3840 x 2160, and 4096 x 2160 (Page 29)
- Vertical frequencies listed are 60, 72, and 75 Hz for most signals, with 30 Hz for 3840 x 2160 (Page 29)
- Interfaces include DVI, VGA, SDI, DP 1.2, HDMI 1.4, and HDMI 2.0 (Page 29)
- A missing pixel does not constitute an out-of-spec defective product (Page 30)
- To resolve power-on issues, turn off the power supply and check that the AC or DC cord is securely inserted (Page 30)
- Image appearance may be delayed due to digital signal processing when turning on, switching inputs, or using "Multi Window" mode (Page 30)
- Spots on the screen can result from electrical distortion from vehicles, trains, high voltage lines, or fluorescent lamps (Page 30)
- When using video software with a screen wider than one in 16:9 mode, blank areas form at the top and bottom of the screen (Page 30)
- Image contour flickering is a normal characteristic of the display control and not a breakdown (Page 30)
- The POWER indicator flashing orange requires checking the number of flashes and contacting the dealer (Page 30)
- The document compares two monitor models: M270TF-XX (27") and M320TF-XX (32") (Page 31)
- Both models feature LED Backlight Technology, TFT Active-matrix, Widescreen, and optional IPS Technology (Page 31)
- Native resolution is 3840 x 2160 (UHD 4K) for both monitors (Page 31)
- Light intensity is 300 cd/m² (typ.) for the M270TF-XX and 350 cd/m² (typ.) for the M320TF-XX, with an option for 700 cd/m² for both (Page 31)
- Input signals include '3G SDI*, 'HDMI 2.0, 'Dual DVI in, 'DP 1.2, 'HDMI 1.4, and 'Audio In (Page 31)
- Output signals include 'DP (Multi-Stream Transport), 'Audio Out, '5V out, and '3G SDI (Loop Through) (Page 31)
- The M270TF-XX weighs 9.5 Kg (20.9 lbs) and the M320TF-XX weighs 11 Kg (24.2 lbs) (Page 31)
- The document includes a note recommending specific cables for SDI connections (Page 31)

The Monitor is a widenscreen, high-definition, healthcare grade display for use during minimally invasive surgical procedures and is suitable for hospital operating rooms, surgical centers, clinics, doctors' offices and similar healthcare environments.
3.3 For Customers in the U.S.A

This equipment has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class B digital device, pursuant to part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference when the equipment is operated in a commercial environment. This equipment uses and can radiate radio frequency energy and, if not installed and used in accordance with the instruction manual, may cause harmful interference to radio communications.
All interface cables used to connect peripherals must be shielded to comply with the limits for a digital device pursuant to Subpart B of part 15 of FCC Rules.
This device complies with part 15 of the FCC Rules. Operation is subject to the following two conditions:
3.4 Customers outside the U.S.A
This product has been manufactured by Winmate Inc.

Inquiries related to product compliance based on European Union legislation shall be addressed to the authorized representative, Winmate. For any service or guarantee matters, please refer to the addresses provided in the separate service or guarantee documents.

This page (Page 20) presents a comprehensive table detailing the electromagnetic immunity requirements for the M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX devices. The table outlines five specific immunity tests—Electrostatic Discharge (ESD), Electrical Fast Transient/Burst, Surge, Voltage Dips/Interruptions, and Power Frequency Magnetic Field—along with their corresponding IEC test levels, compliance levels, and environmental guidance. The document specifies that the equipment is intended for use in typical commercial or hospital environments and provides detailed recommendations for maintaining proper operating conditions, such as floor material, humidity, and power quality. A note at the bottom clarifies that the test level refers to the A.C. mains voltage prior to application.

**Text Evidence:**
- The M270TF-XXX / M320TF-XXX is intended for use in an electromagnetic environment specified below.
- For ESD, the test level is ±6 kV contact and ±8 kV air, with compliance required at the same levels.
- For Electrical Fast Transient/Burst, the test level is ±2 kV for power supply lines and ±1 kV for input/output lines.
- For Surge, the test level is ±1 kV line-to-line and ±2 kV line-to-earth.
- For Voltage Dips, Short Interruptions, and Voltage Variations, the test levels are <5% dip for 0.5 cycle, 40% dip for 5 cycles, and 70% dip for 25 cycles.
- For Power Frequency Magnetic Field, the test level is 3 A/m.
- The customer or user should assure the device is used in the specified environment.
- If continued operation during power interruptions is required, it is recommended to power the device from an uninterruptible power supply or battery.

Warning on power connection: Use a proper power cord for your local power supply. Use the approved Power Cord (3-core mains lead) / Appliance Connector /Plug with earthing-contacts that conforms to the safety regulations of each country if applicable. Use the Power Cord (3-core mains lead) / Appliance Connector / Plug conforming to the proper ratings (Voltage, Ampere). pages.summary:
This page (Page 26) from Chapter 3 provides important safety and maintenance information for a healthcare use LCD monitor. It details potential causes of screen burn-in, including static images with non-16:9 aspect ratios and continuous character displays, and offers preventative measures like turning off connected equipment. The section on the screen protect panel warns that while it is made of toughened glass, it can crack if dropped or scratched. The document also explains moisture condensation risks when moving the unit between temperature extremes and advises turning it off until the condensation clears. Finally, it provides specific cleaning instructions, emphasizing the use of disinfectant-resistant materials and safe alcohol concentrations (50-70% isopropyl or 76.9-81.4% ethanol) while avoiding harsh chemicals.

**Text Evidence:**
- Burn-in can be caused by masked/boarded images with aspect ratios other than 16:9, color bars, or continuous characters.
- To reduce burn-in risk, turn off character displays from connected equipment.
- The screen protect panel is made of toughened glass but may crack from strong impact or scratching.
- Moisture condensation occurs when the unit moves from cold to warm environments; operating during condensation may damage the unit.
- Cleaning requires disconnecting the AC power cord before starting.
- The front protection plate withstands disinfection and is treated to reduce light reflection.
- Use 50-70% isopropyl alcohol or 76.9-81.4% ethanol for cleaning, wiping with less than 1 N force.
- Avoid solvents like benzene, thinners, acid, alkaline, abrasive detergents, or chemical cleaning cloths.

This page (Page 29) from the 4K UHD Display User Manual presents Section 3.9, titled "Troubleshooting," which is a table listing common display issues and their corresponding solutions. The table covers problems such as dead pixels, power-on failures, image delay, screen spots, color issues, flickering, and a flashing orange POWER indicator. It provides specific troubleshooting steps for each issue, including checking cable connections, adjusting input configurations like "RGB"/"YPBPR", and understanding that certain visual effects are normal characteristics of the display technology. The section also notes that missing pixels are not considered defective products.

**Text Evidence:**
- A missing pixel does not constitute an out-of-spec defective product.
- To resolve power-on issues, turn off the power supply and check that the AC or DC cord is securely inserted.
- Image appearance may be delayed due to digital signal processing when turning on, switching inputs, or using "Multi Window" mode.
- Spots on the screen can result from electrical distortion from vehicles, trains, high voltage lines, or fluorescent lamps.
- When using video software with a screen wider than one in 16:9 mode, blank areas form at the top and bottom of the screen.
- Image contour flickering is a normal characteristic of the display control and not a breakdown.
- The POWER indicator flashing orange requires checking the number of flashes and contacting the dealer.

- Page 31: The document compares two monitor models: M270TF-XX (27") and M320TF-XX (32"), both with UHD 4K resolution (3840 x 2160), LED Backlight Technology, TFT Active-matrix, Widescreen, and optional IPS Technology. Light intensity is 300 cd/m² (typ.) for M270TF-XX and 350 cd/m² (typ.) for M320TF-XX, with an option for 700 cd/m² for both. Input signals include 3G SDI, HDMI 2.0, Dual DVI in, DP 1.2, HDMI 1.4, and Audio In. Output signals include DP (Multi-Stream Transport), Audio Out, 5V out, and 3G SDI (Loop Through). The M270TF-XX weighs 9.5 Kg (20.9 lbs) and the M320TF-XX weighs 11 Kg (24.2 lbs). A note recommends specific cables for SDI connections. (Page 31)
- Page 32: The device has factory options including 'Rubber Bumper' and 'Projected Capacitive Multitouch, USB touch screen'. Operating temperature is 0°C to 35°C with humidity up to 95%. Storage temperature is -20°C to 60°C with humidity up to 95%. The IP rating is front IP65 and rear IP22. The document recommends using 75 Ohm RG59 cable or above for HD-SDI and 75Ohm RG6 cable for 3G-SDI. Data rates are listed as SD-SDI 270 Mb/sec, HD-SDI 1.485 Mb/sec, and 3G-SDI 2.97Mb/sec. (Page 32)
- Page 33: The AC adapter accepts an input of AC 100 V – 240 V at 50 Hz/60 Hz with a current draw of up to 1.2 A. The device has a weight of approximately 0.7 kg (1.5 lbs). Operating conditions specify an ambient temperature of 5°C – 35°C, with a recommended range of 20°C – 30°C. The protection class against electric shock is Class I. Storage and transport conditions allow for an ambient temperature of -20°C – 60°C and relative humidity of 10% – 85%. (Page 33)
- Page 34: The document is titled "PIN Specification" and details the pin assignment and signal names for three terminals: RS-232 C, HD15, and GPI. Specific signal names include CD, TXD, RXD, DSR, GND, DTR, CTS, RTS, RI, R, G, B, SDA, HD/SYNC, VD, SCL, DGND, and RJ11_GPIO_x. Notes indicate that certain pins are not connected (NC) or require a short circuit to another pin on the monitor. (Page 34)
- Page 35: The page details the pin assignment and signal names for DVI-D, DP-IN, and DP-Out connectors. Pin 1 of the DVI-D connector is assigned to DVI_RX2-. Pin 15 of the DVI-D connector is assigned to DVI_CON_CABLE_DETECT. The DP-IN and DP-Out connectors both use a 20-pin configuration with similar signal assignments, including four lanes (Lane 0-3), AUX, Hot Plug, and DP_PWR. Several pins are designated as "NC" (No Connect). (Page 35)
- Page 36: Pin assignment and signal name for SDI-IN, SDI-Out, HDMI, USB, and Power are provided. The HDMI connector has 19 pins, with specific signals like HDMI_DET, HDMI_D2P, HDMI_D2M, HDMI_D1P, HDMI_D1M, HDMI_D0P, HDMI_D0M, HDMI_CLKP, HDMI_CLKM, HDMI_CEC_OUT, DDC_CLOCK, and DDC_DATA. The USB connector has pins for +5V, Data+, Data-, and GND. The Power connector has pins for +5V and GND. (Page 36)
- Page 37: The document is from Appendix A: Technical Specification, page 36. It presents dimensional figures for a 27" Model and a 32" Model. Dimensions are provided in both millimeters and inches (e.g., 643.17 mm / 25.3"). Both models have a depth of 48.00 mm (1.8") and feature a VESA mounting pattern. (Page 37)
- Page 38: The document is titled "Appendix B: Meaning of Symbols on the unit" from the "4K UHD Display User Manual". The table lists symbols such as the potential equalization terminal, CE mark, and TUV SUD Mark. Descriptions include compliance with the Healthcare Device Directive 93/42/EEC, UL Listing Mark, and FCC compliance (Part 15, Class B). Specific symbols like "Keep away from rain" and "Indicates user need to read user manual before using the device" are included. (Page 38)

The table outlines key technical specifications including screen technology, viewable size (27" and 32" diagonal), native resolution (UHD 4K for both), pixel pitch, light intensity, contrast ratio, input/output signals, power requirements, dimensions, weight, and mounting options. It also lists various product features, operating temperatures, and compliance certifications. A note at the bottom specifies cable recommendations for SDI connections.

**Text Evidence:**
- The document compares two monitor models: M270TF-XX (27") and M320TF-XX (32").
- Both models feature LED Backlight Technology, TFT Active-matrix, Widescreen, and optional IPS Technology.
- Native resolution is 3840 x 2160 (UHD 4K) for both monitors.
- Light intensity is 300 cd/m² (typ.) for the M270TF-XX and 350 cd/m² (typ.) for the M320TF-XX, with an option for 700 cd/m² for both.
- Input signals include '3G SDI*, 'HDMI 2.0, 'Dual DVI in, 'DP 1.2, 'HDMI 1.4, and 'Audio In.
- Output signals include 'DP (Multi-Stream Transport), 'Audio Out, '5V out, and '3G SDI (Loop Through).
- The M270TF-XX weighs 9.5 Kg (20.9 lbs) and the M320TF-XX weighs 11 Kg (24.2 lbs).
- The document includes a note recommending specific cables for SDI connections.

**Visual Evidence:**
<table_summary>Table: Monitor - This table provides a side-by-side comparison of the technical specifications for the M270TF-XX and M320TF-XX monitors, covering aspects like Screen Technology, Viewable Size, Native Resolution, Pixel Pitch, Light Intensity, Contrast Ratio, Input/Output Signals, Power Specifications, Dimensions, Weight, and Mounting.</table_summary>

This page from the 4K UHD Display User Manual (page 31) provides technical specifications for a display device, including factory options, operating and storage temperature ranges, IP ratings, and type approvals. The main content is a comprehensive table detailing SDI resolution, frame rate, and cable requirements, which lists various resolutions like 1920x1080 and 1280x720 with corresponding frame rates (e.g., 60/P, 50/I) and recommended cables (RG59, RG6). A note at the bottom specifies that 75 Ohm RG59 or above should be used for HD-SDI and 75Ohm RG6 for 3G-SDI. The page also includes a list of data transmission rates for different SDI standards.

**Text Evidence:**
- The device has factory options including 'Rubber Bumper' and 'Projected Capacitive Multitouch, USB touch screen'.
- Operating temperature is 0°C to 35°C with humidity up to 95%.
- Storage temperature is -20°C to 60°C with humidity up to 95%.
- The IP rating is front IP65 and rear IP22.
- The document recommends using 75 Ohm RG59 cable or above for HD-SDI and 75Ohm RG6 cable for 3G-SDI.
- Data rates are listed as SD-SDI 270 Mb/sec, HD-SDI 1.485 Mb/sec, and 3G-SDI 2.97Mb/sec.

**Visual Evidence:**
<table_summary>Table 1: Factory Options, Operating Temperature, Storage Temperature, IP Rating, Type Approval, Testing and Certificates - This table compares two configurations side-by-side, listing features such as rubber bumper, projected capacitive multitouch, operating temperature (0°C to 35°C), storage temperature (-20°C to 60°C), IP rating (front IP65 - rear IP22), and a long list of international standards and compliance certifications.</table_summary>
<table_summary>Table 2: SDI Resolution, frame rate and cable - This table details the required SDI cable types for various video resolutions and frame rates. It includes entries for 1920x1080 resolution with frame rates of 60/P, 50/P, 60/I, 50/I, 30/P, 25/P, 24/P, 30/PsF, and 25/PsF, all requiring either RG6 or RG59/RG6 cables. It also covers 1280x720 resolution with 60/P and 50/P frame rates, requiring RG58, RG59, or RG6 cables.</table_summary>

This page (Page 34) provides technical specifications for three different display connectors: DVI-D, DP-IN, and DP-Out. It includes a diagram of the DVI-D connector and detailed tables listing the pin number and corresponding signal name for each pin. The tables cover differential signals like DVI_RX0+, DVI_RX0-, Lane 0, Lane 1, etc., as well as power, ground, and control signals such as +5V_DVI, GND, AUX, Hot Plug, and DP_PWR. The information is presented in a structured format with clear headings for each connector type.

**Text Evidence:**
- The page details the pin assignment and signal names for DVI-D, DP-IN, and DP-Out connectors.
- Pin 1 of the DVI-D connector is assigned to DVI_RX2-.
- Pin 15 of the DVI-D connector is assigned to DVI_CON_CABLE_DETECT.
- The DP-IN and DP-Out connectors both use a 20-pin configuration with similar signal assignments, including four lanes (Lane 0-3), AUX, Hot Plug, and DP_PWR.
- Several pins are designated as "NC" (No Connect).

A disclaimer from Winmate states they can change product specifications or discontinue products without notice. - In some countries, products can be returned to a local retailer upon purchase of an equivalent new product.
